pr.title: Plan the keyboard instrument: field keys with keymaps, a SuperCollider voice host, and recorded keys
pr.head: 163260514d21a4d9f0a497b72bcb74e2a91a6a8d

summary: Field is a command-line music production tool whose songs live in Git. Today it makes sound only by rendering: a SuperCollider program under shared/instruments/ runs offline from a seed and a duration and writes one WAV file. Nothing in Field takes notes. No code opens a MIDI input, the audio daemon field-audiod hands every hosted plugin an empty MIDI buffer, and no command reads the keyboard as anything but commands. So you cannot hear how an instrument responds under your fingers, which is how a player judges one.
This pull request adds one file, the plan docs/projects/keyboard-instrument/readme.md, and changes no code. The plan designs four chunks, each meant to be one later pull request:

1. field keys as a MIDI device. The command reads key presses and releases from the terminal, finds the physical key behind each one, looks it up in a keymap file, and sends the result from a virtual MIDI source named Field Keys, which Logic or any other application can play from.
  2. The voice host. field keys <instrument> also starts sclang, SuperCollider's language process, which boots its own scsynth audio server and plays the instrument's new voice mode from every MIDI source.
  3. Two more built-in keymaps. tracker and fourths join the default, Logic's Musical Typing.
  4. Recording. The daemon timestamps played notes against the song's transport, and the build renders the take offline through the same voice. Its file format and two other questions stay open until that chunk starts.

The plan is marked status: ready, which in this repository's Projector convention claims that the work can start. That claim covers chunks 1 to 3. The review left four findings open: a wrong section citation, a sample-rate conflict with field play, a missing (DECIDED) marker, and an acceptance criterion that cannot fail for the behavior it checks. Each appears as a flag under the line it concerns.

cards.title: Terms this page uses
cards.html:
• Position: a physical key, named by its W3C KeyboardEvent.code value such as KeyA or Semicolon. The name comes from the US key in that place, but it means the place, whatever the key types.
  • Keyboard layout: the operating system's map from position to character, such as QWERTY, Dvorak, or AZERTY.
  • Keymap: Field's YAML map from position to what the key plays: a note, a chord, or a control such as transpose or sustain.
  • Kitty keyboard protocol: a terminal extension that reports key releases and repeats, which ordinary terminals do not. Ghostty and iTerm2 3.5 and later implement it. Apple's Terminal does not.
  • Base layout key: an optional field of that protocol that names the US key at the pressed position. A terminal leaves it out when it equals the typed key.
  • Helper: the new short-lived field-audiod --keys mode. It publishes the virtual MIDI source and reports the active keyboard layout on macOS.
  • Voice host: an sclang process that boots scsynth on the output device and turns MIDI into voices.
  • Voice mode: the second way to run an instrument program. With FIELD_MODE=voice, the program returns one SynthDef with freq, amp, and gate controls instead of rendering a file.

groups.title: The keyboard-instrument plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: field keys, keymaps, a SuperCollider voice host, and recorded keys
intro: The whole pull request is this plan. It reads top to bottom in the order the repository's plans use: the problem, the solution, the reasons for the design, acceptance criteria, cost, rollout, open questions, and background.

1. §1 and §2: what is missing and the design. §2.1 walks one key press from the terminal to sound. §2.2 to §2.5 cover the terminal protocol, how a key's position is found, the keymap format, and the native helper. §2.6 is the contract an instrument answers to be playable, and §2.7 sketches recording.
  2. §3: why this design. Each bullet names the design that was chosen and the alternatives it beat, such as a virtual MIDI device instead of sending straight to SuperCollider, and the kitty protocol instead of guessing releases from key repeat.
  3. §4: acceptance criteria. Criteria 1 to 29 are checked by hand, chunk by chunk, and a list of vitest files fails before the change.
  4. §5 to §8. Latency estimates, the four-chunk rollout, eight open questions, and the background research the design rests on.
Read the four flags first. Each marks a finding the review left open, under the line it concerns. The verified notes record claims about the existing code that the review checked against this head.

files.note: The new plan, at status: ready and priority: now.

checks.text: status: ready claims the plan can be built. Chunk 4's design is left to the start of that chunk, which §6 item 4 says explicitly, so the claim covers chunks 1 to 3 only.

This citation, and the ones at lines 523 and 549, name project-layout.md §1 decision 6, which is "One ledger per scope". The decision the plan means, that one .scd renders from a spec or plays from notes depending on how it is invoked, is §4 decision 6, cited elsewhere in the repository as project-layout.md §4.6. The pull request body repeats the wrong citation.

Three words carry the rest of the plan: position (the physical key), keyboard layout (what the key types), and keymap (what the key plays). Keep them apart while you read, because the design looks up positions and never characters.

The terminal handshake: probe for the kitty protocol, push flags 1, 2, 4, and 8 so that letter keys report releases and the base layout key, turn on focus reports, and undo both on every exit path. A focus-out releases every held note, because a terminal that lost focus never reports the release.

Position comes from two sources. The terminal's base layout key wins when it is present. Otherwise field keys looks the typed character up in the keyboard layout the helper read from macOS. Neither source alone is enough, because a missing base layout key could mean a QWERTY layout or a terminal that never sends one.

The note counts are ranges of distinct pitches, and they hold. Musical Typing binds offsets 0 to 17, which is 18 notes. The standard FastTracker 2 layout that tracker follows spans offsets 0 to 31 across its two rows, which is 32, and criterion 28's 48, 60, and 72 fall on it. The fourths grid spans 0 to 26, which is 27. Checked by working out each keymap's offsets by hand.

Review suggestion: on macOS a Node watch on a file stays with the original file, so an editor that saves by renaming a temporary file over the keymap ends the watch after the first save. Watching the keymap's directory avoids that.

The fourths values hold: with column: 1 and row: 5, KeyZ is offset 0 (48), KeyA 5 (53), KeyQ 10 (58), and Digit1 15 (63). Criterion 29's chords also check out: KeyZ, KeyB, KeyD give 48, 52, 55, and one key to the right gives 49, 53, 56.

Review suggestion: this rule should say that a release always ends the notes its press started, whatever modifiers it carries, and that the Caps Lock and Num Lock bits, which flag 8 reports on every key, are ignored. Without that, a key released while Ctrl is held could leave its note stuck.

The helper lives exactly as long as its input pipe. When field keys exits for any reason, even kill -9, the pipe closes, the helper removes Field Keys, and exits. All note logic stays in TypeScript, where vitest covers it without the native build.

The voice contract asks an instrument for one SynthDef with SuperCollider's standard event controls. The voice host owns sustain, pitch bend, and voice stealing, so an instrument needs only a gated envelope that frees itself.

This holds only in one order. field play <song> moves the output device to the song's rate whenever the device can switch (maybeMatchDeviceRate in native/audiod/src/player.cpp). Start criterion 21 on a device at 44.1 kHz and then field play creek, and the device moves to bloom's 48 kHz under the running scsynth. Criterion 25 at line 611 then fails, and the plan does not say what the voice host does.

runScProgram in src/generators/supercollider.ts already prints the last 15 non-empty lines of sclang's standard output on failure, because sclang reports errors there. Checked by reading the function.

The code these rows build on exists with the roles the plan gives it: daemonBinary() in src/audiod/client.ts, programPath() in src/generators/supercollider.ts, and the sclang lookup order FIELD_SCLANG, then PATH, then the app bundle, inside runScProgram. Checked by reading both files.

docs/projects/README.md asks for settled decisions to be marked (DECIDED), and AGENTS.md tells agents not to reopen one so marked. This section records each choice with the alternatives it beat but carries no marker, unlike playback.md, multi-rate.md, and remote.md.
The control plane has three runtime dependencies, commander, yaml, and zod, none of them native. Checked in package.json.
Review suggestion: keymap names do not quite follow programPath()'s rule. §2.4 treats a name ending in .yaml as a path, while programPath() treats any name without a / as bare.

This is the only check that the helper re-reads the keyboard layout mid-session, but in Ghostty both keys arrive with a base layout key, so the helper's second report is never used. A helper that never notices the input-source change still passes. Switching to U.S. International – PC mid-session and expecting Quote to be named as dead would test the helper in any terminal.

Review suggestion: this keymap sounds note 60 from both KeyA and KeyF. The plan does not say what releasing one does while the other is held, so the session could cut a note the other key still holds.
field sc render <program> takes --seed, --duration, and --output, as this criterion uses them. Checked in src/cli.ts.

Every open question names what it waits for. Questions 1 to 3 wait for the start of chunk 4. Questions 4 to 8 wait for another project, for play experience, or for a need, so none blocks the ready claim for chunks 1 to 3.

No MIDI input exists today. A search of src/, native/, and python/ finds no CoreMIDI or MidiInput use, and native/audiod/src/hosting.cpp passes an empty juce::MidiBuffer, declared in hosting.h, to processBlock.
still-water-pad.scd renders four chord tones with three detuned voices each under Env.linen, and its voice is one SynthDef, \stillWaterVoice. Checked by reading the file in examples/bloom.
